# What exact operator structure buys: the linear suites {#sec-linear-suites}

On linear boundary-value problems with exact labels, an architecture
whose decoder evaluates the exact singular kernel of the governing
operator beats a 27x-larger physics-agnostic Transolver in every regime
tested, generalizes across boundary-condition frequency content where
soft-slice attention and separable decoders do not, and extrapolates
boundary-data amplitude exactly because linearity is declared rather
than learned. This chapter collects those measurements, organized by
question rather than by suite, and closes with the places the exact
kernel is not available.

The architecture throughout is the exact-kernel MeshTransformer
(MT1 after this point; @sec-mt1): one or two boundary self-attention
layers that produce an operator state per boundary cell, and a decoder
that writes the interior field at a query point $x$ as a sum over
boundary cells $j$,

$$
u(x) = \sum_j \kappa(x, y_j)\, V_j,
\qquad
\kappa(x, y_j) = \sum_m C_m(\mathrm{op}_j)\, \varphi_m(x, y_j),
$$

where $\varphi_m$ are dictionary members integrated exactly over each
cell (the double-layer member is the signed subtended angle in 2D and
the signed solid angle in 3D; the single-layer member is the Hess–Smith
segment form in 2D and a per-edge $\operatorname{asinh}$ form in 3D),
$C_m$ are coefficients that depend on the encoded operator state of the
source cell, and $V_j$ is the drive-linear value state (@sec-kernel-decoder,
@sec-decoder-role). The reference configuration has 82k–105k
parameters depending on dictionary and depth. Its contracts are
similarity equivariance through an intrinsic gauge (@sec-intrinsic-gauge),
drive linearity when declared, parity-typed channels, and bitwise
query independence.

```{python}

INK, INK2, MUTED, GRID, BASELINE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#898781", "#e1e0d9", "#c3c2b7"

                     "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID,
```

## The linear suites at a glance

Three exactly solvable families carry the evidence. Each has closed-form
labels (no solver in the loop), online training data (a fresh random case
per optimizer step, so there is no finite training set to memorize), and
frozen evaluation banks that each move one factor away from the training
distribution. Dataset construction and split definitions are in
@sec-datasets; the table names what this chapter uses.

| suite | equation | domains | labels | evaluation banks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2D Laplace | $\Delta u = 0$, Dirichlet | conformal images of the disk (Laurent modes $\{2,3\}$, certified injective) with random similarity placement | $u = \operatorname{Re} H(z)$, exactly harmonic | interpolation; unseen geometry modes $\{4,5\}$; stronger deformation; mixed modes; unseen boundary frequencies (zero-mean modes 5–8 vs 1–4); 64 cases each |
| 2D Laplace, hard geometry | $\Delta u = 0$, Dirichlet | multi-body (disk minus two disks) and deep-cavity (slotted disk) | exterior point charges | in-distribution, narrow gap, single body, unseen charge count; deep slot, convex control |
| screened Laplace | $\Delta u - \kappa^2 u = 0$, Dirichlet | random disks; $\tilde\kappa = \kappa R \in [0.5, 2]$ as a global operator scalar | modified-Bessel series | in-distribution; $\tilde\kappa \in [3,5]$; $\tilde\kappa \in [0.05, 0.3]$; unseen drive modes $\{4,5,6\}$ |
| 3D Laplace | $\Delta u = 0$, Dirichlet (mixed on shells) | icosphere-based spheres, spherical-harmonic stars, two-surface shells | exterior point charges | sphere; star; star with unseen deformation modes; shell (multiply connected) |
| exterior potential flow | $\Delta\psi = 0$ outside a body, uniform stream $U_\infty$, circulation $\Gamma$ | certified exterior conformal bodies | closed-form streamfunction and velocity | in-distribution; unseen geometry; wilder shapes; circulation beyond training; far-field queries |

: The linear suites. "Unseen boundary frequencies" is the sharpest
split: it asks whether the learned operator transfers to right-hand
sides whose harmonic content was never seen, and its zero-mean
construction prevents a correctly reproduced constant from masking
interior error. {#tbl-linear-suites}

![The 2D Laplace training family (top) and two of its evaluation
axes: unseen shape modes at the training deformation range (middle) and
stronger deformation of the trained modes (bottom). Boundaries are
colored by the Dirichlet trace, diverging about each sample's boundary
mean. Not shown: the random similarity placement (rotation, reflection,
translation, scale in $[0.2, 5]$) every case carries.
`figures/gallery_2d.png`.](figures/gallery_2d.png){#fig-gallery2d}

The error measure everywhere in this chapter is the relative $L^2$
error of the predicted interior field over the query points of one
case, $\|\hat u - u\| / \|u\|$, averaged over the cases of a bank. A
predictor that returns zero scores 1.0; the boundary-mean predictor
scores 0.80 on 2D Laplace interpolation and 1.0 on the unseen-frequency
bank.^[`results/reference_2026-07-01.json`, block `accuracy`.]

### The 2D Laplace suite {#sec-ds-laplace2d}

Domains are images of the unit disk under $F(z) = z + \sum_m a_m z^m$
with injectivity certificate $\sum_m m|a_m| < 1$; drives are harmonic
polynomials in the disk frame, so the interior solution is available at
any point in closed form. The training family uses shape modes
$\{2,3\}$, deformation bound in $[0.05, 0.35]$ and drive modes 1–4. The
hard-geometry extension keeps the exact physics and changes the
geometry to families where two boundary points can be close in
$\mathbb R^2$ while the field between them is mediated by the whole
domain (@sec-encoder-stress).

### The screened suite {#sec-ds-screened}

The modified-Helmholtz equation $\Delta u - \kappa^2 u = 0$ on random
disks is the program's one parametric linear family. The dimensionless
screening $\tilde\kappa = \kappa R$ enters MT1 only as a global operator
scalar that conditions the encoder and, through it, the kernel
coefficients; the dictionary itself is not told what $\tilde\kappa$
means. Two banks push the parameter above and below the training band,
a third moves the drive spectrum at fixed parameter.

### The 3D Laplace suite {#sec-ds-laplace3d}

Exterior point charges give exact harmonic labels on any closed
triangulated surface. Three tiers vary shape and connectivity
(@sec-3d-suite): spheres of random radius and orientation; stars,
$r(\hat u) = R(1 + \sum \varepsilon\, Y_{lm}(\hat u))$ over low-degree
real spherical harmonics with degree-4 modes held out; and shells, an
outer surface plus an inward-oriented inner surface with charges in the
cavity, so the solution carries net flux through the domain. The 3D
generator assigns boundary-condition types per surface, which makes the
shell the one tier on which a mixed Dirichlet–Neumann problem can be
posed (@sec-mixed-bc).

#### Tiers and the shell {#sec-3d-suite}

The shell tier exists to change what a kernel dictionary must
represent. A double-layer potential integrates to zero net flux through
any closed surface, so a double-layer-only dictionary cannot carry the
monopole component $u \sim a + b/r$ that cavity charges induce; the
single-layer member can. A parameter-free oracle (the exact solid-angle
double layer with a dense second-kind solve) reads 0.003 on spheres,
0.002 on stars and 0.753 on shells on the banks used below:^[`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`,
key `iteration_10_laplace3d_meshtransformer`, setup block.] the shell
number is a representation fact, not an optimization failure.

### The headline: against a physics-agnostic Transolver {#sec-linear-headline}

Transolver (@sec-transolver) is the strongest physics-agnostic
attention architecture for PDE surrogacy in this program's comparison
set. The port is verified against the official implementation and given
a shared boundary+query token sequence, so its queries attend to each
other, which is more interaction than MT1's query-independent decoder
allows. Both sides train on the identical streaming protocol: one fresh
case per step, AdamW at $3\times10^{-4}$, seeds 17/29/43, the same
frozen banks. Two Transolver capacities are run: matched (103,053
parameters against MT1's 104,261) and native (2,809,409; 27x). The
archive records parameters and steps but not peak training memory for
these runs; MT1's dense decode costs $O(N_q N_s)$ per case, so the
matched-parameter comparison is not a matched-FLOP one.

| model | parameters | steps | 2D Laplace ID | unseen frequencies | similarity covariance |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Transolver, matched | 103,053 | 3,000 | 0.769 | 1.00 | 0.06–0.13 |
| Transolver, native | 2,809,409 | 3,000 | 0.608 | 0.97 | 0.10–0.25 |
| Transolver, native | 2,809,409 | 10,000 | 0.262 | 0.77 | 0.18–0.21 |
| Transolver, native | 2,809,409 | 30,000 | 0.119 | 0.46 | 0.08–0.11 |
| MT1, singular-only dictionary | 104,261 | 3,000 | **0.0375** | **0.0748** | $3\times10^{-7}$ |

: Three-seed means on the frozen 2D Laplace banks. Similarity
covariance is the relative disagreement between predictions on a case
and on its rotated, reflected, translated and rescaled copy, measured
on the trained checkpoints. `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`,
key `iteration_15_transolver_comparison`. {#tbl-transolver-linear}

```{python}
#| label: fig-transolver-steps
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Transolver's in-distribution error against online training steps
#|   (log-log). Grey lines: native capacity (2.8M parameters), one line
#|   style per seed. Grey open markers: matched capacity (103k) at 3,000
#|   steps, one marker shape per seed. Purple dashed line: MT1 with the
#|   singular-only dictionary at 3,000 steps (0.0375). After 10x the
#|   compute and 27x the parameters Transolver remains 3.2x above the MT1
#|   reference. Not shown: the unseen-frequency bank, where native
#|   Transolver saturates near 0.46 at 30,000 steps.
#|   results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json, key iteration_15_transolver_comparison.
#| code-fold: true
it15 = BIE["iteration_15_transolver_comparison"]
native = {}
matched = {}
for run in it15["runs_3000"] + it15["runs_step_curve"]:
    if run["parameters"] > 1_000_000:
        native.setdefault(run["seed"], []).append((run["steps"], run["ID"]))
    else:
        matched[run["seed"]] = (run["steps"], run["ID"])
reference = it15["reference_MT_singonly_3000steps"]["ID"]

styles = {17: "-", 29: "--", 43: ":"}
markers = {17: "o", 29: "s", 43: "^"}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.0))
for seed, points in sorted(native.items()):
    points.sort()
    ax.plot([p[0] for p in points], [p[1] for p in points], styles[seed],
            color=GREY, lw=1.6, marker=markers[seed], ms=6, mfc=GREY,
            mec="white", mew=1.0,
            label=f"Transolver, native (2.8M), seed {seed}")
for seed, (steps, value) in sorted(matched.items()):
    ax.plot(steps, value, markers[seed], color=GREY, ms=8, mfc="white",
            mec=GREY, mew=1.6,
            label=f"Transolver, matched (103k), seed {seed}")
ax.axhline(reference, color=PURPLE, lw=1.8, ls="--",
           label="MT1, singular-only (104k), 3,000 steps")
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xlim(2.2e3, 4.5e4)
ax.set_ylim(0.02, 1.2)
ax.set_xlabel("online training steps [log]")
ax.set_ylabel("in-distribution relative $L^2$ [log]")
ax.legend(fontsize=7.5, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.2), ncol=2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The same gap holds in Transolver's own regime. On a fixed dataset of
4,608 finite-element-verified 2D cases (random Fourier Dirichlet traces
in arc length; solver labels at relative error $\sim10^{-8}$; 2,304
training cases; 15 epochs; best-checkpoint selection; seeds 17/29), MT1
reaches 0.016–0.017 in distribution and 0.010–0.013 on unseen trace
frequencies; matched Transolver reads 0.126–0.136 and 0.112–0.131,
native Transolver 0.062–0.070 and 0.089–0.108.^[`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`,
keys `iteration_17_fixed_dataset_regime` and
`iteration_15_transolver_comparison/screened_and_3d_extension`.] The
solver-verified labels also show that MT1 is not exploiting the
manufactured-solution construction of the exact-label suites. Across
the remaining suites at matched parameters and three seeds, the
ratio of Transolver's error to MT1's is 78x on screened Laplace
(0.773 vs 0.0099), 56x on 3D spheres, 34x on stars, 6.8x on stars with
unseen modes, and 1.4x on shells (0.529 vs 0.377). The gap narrows
exactly where MT1's own dictionary is representation-limited and widens
where the exact kernel applies.

## What exact operator structure buys {#sec-part-accuracy}

The accuracy of MT1 on these suites lives in two exact singular kernel
members with operator-conditioned coefficients. Everything else that
could have carried it (smooth dictionary members, a second attention
layer, multiple heads, vector channels on easy geometry, an external
length scale) was priced by ablation and kept only where measurement
keeps it. This section gives the evidence, starting from the known-PDE
oracle that shows what the ceiling is.

### A three-parameter learned boundary-integral solve {#sec-ladder}

When the PDE is known, a learned operator can be built from exactly the
ingredients of a boundary-integral method and nothing else, and the
result recovers the classical double-layer kernel from interior data.
The ingredient ablation below uses one seed (17), 1,000 updates and an
early 8-case bank per split; the control is a free-form pair kernel, an
MLP of the joint invariants $(|r|^2, n\cdot r)$ with 19,008 parameters.

| model | parameters | ID | unseen geometry | stronger deformation | unseen frequencies | boundary trace | Laplacian residual |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| free-form pair kernel (control) | 19,008 | 0.091 | 0.101 | 0.124 | 0.605 | 0.150 | 8.0 |
| MLP kernel inside a Richardson density solve | 19,008 | 0.154 | — | — | 0.756 | — | — |
| exact harmonic basis, midpoint quadrature, solve | 13 | 0.652 | — | — | 1.014 | 0.002 | $\approx 0$ |
| exact harmonic basis, direct (no solve), exact panel quadrature | 5 | 0.213 | 0.222 | 0.194 | 0.352 | 0.359 | $\approx 0$ |
| **exact basis + exact panel quadrature + learned solve** | **13** | **0.035** | **0.038** | **0.055** | **0.090** | 0.0004 | $\approx 0$ |
| analytic Richardson oracle | 8 | 0.003 | 0.003 | 0.026 | 0.060 | 0.0005 | $\approx 0$ |

: Ingredient ablation of the learned boundary-integral solve on 2D
Laplace (seed 17, 1,000 updates, early bank). "Laplacian residual" is
the normalized autograd residual $\|L^2\Delta \hat u\|/\|\hat u\|$;
"boundary trace" is the relative error of the predicted field's limit
at the boundary against the Dirichlet data. `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`,
block `hypothesis_chain`. {#tbl-h1e}

Three ingredients are each necessary and none sufficient. A density
solve wrapped around a free-form kernel is worse than the kernel alone
(0.756 on unseen frequencies): the solve exerts no pressure toward
trace consistency. An exactly harmonic basis under midpoint quadrature
loses to the free-form MLP (0.652 in distribution): singular kernels
cannot mollify quadrature error next to a panel, so the optimizer
suppresses the singular coefficient. With every basis term integrated in
closed form over each panel (the singular term reduces to the signed
subtended angle), a 13-parameter model trained from random
initialization reaches 0.035 in distribution and 0.090 on unseen
frequencies, the level of the analytic operator. Soft penalties on trace
or harmonicity at equal weight move only their own diagnostic.^[Same
artifact, block `ablations_seed17_early_bank`.]

![The learned kernel against the analytic interior double layer
$-\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\, n\cdot r/|r|^2$: angular profile at $|r|=1$ (left),
radial decay (center), and the learned coefficient $c_1$ for three seeds
on the reference bank against $-1/2\pi$ (right). The learned object is
the classical kernel to within 0.8% on every seed, which is what
licenses classical acceleration (fast multipole,
$\mathcal H$-matrices) downstream.
`figures/kernel_learned_vs_analytic.png`.](figures/kernel_learned_vs_analytic.png){#fig-kernel}

#### Pruning: two scalars carry the operator {#sec-pruning}

Sharing one relaxation across the eight Richardson steps and dropping
the regular Laurent orders leaves 3 parameters and the same accuracy to
four decimals (seed 17, 3,000 steps, early bank: 0.0056 in
distribution, 0.0612 on unseen frequencies, versus 0.0062 and 0.0618 for
the 13-parameter model).^[`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, keys
`iteration_4_pruning` and `resolution_transfer_seed17`.] The learned
values are $c_1 = -0.15828$ (0.5% from $-1/2\pi$), $d_0 \approx 0$ and
$\alpha = 1.18$. Cutting the solve to two steps degrades the trace
160x and inflates the kernel to compensate: solve depth is a
numerical-convergence knob, not prunable capacity. On the frozen 64-case
reference bank at 3,000 steps the 3-parameter model reads
$0.0347 \pm 0.0006$ in distribution and $0.0664 \pm 0.0004$ on unseen
frequencies over three seeds, Laplacian residual $10^{-4}$, and it
improves monotonically under boundary refinement from 32 to 256 panels
(0.183 to 0.038) with no retraining.

#### Neumann boundary conditions {#sec-neumann}

The recipe transfers to flux data. The Neumann model adds the
single-layer term $c_0\operatorname{Re}\log\zeta$ with exact panel
integrals and obtains the Neumann trace by autograd differentiation of
those integrals. One design rule is not optional: the orientation gauge
of the second-kind system must place the zero-kernel initialization
inside the solver's convergent regime. In the textbook interior
orientation $-\tfrac12 I + \tilde K'$ with relaxation near $+1$, a zero
kernel makes each Richardson step a $1.49\times$ amplifier, and training
exploits solver divergence as gain (in-distribution 0.081 with a learned
kernel of zero). In the convergent gauge $+\tfrac12 I + \tilde K'$ the
model crosses a co-adaptation barrier (validation rises to 3.4 near step
250) and converges about three times more slowly than Dirichlet: at
10,000 steps, seed 17, in-distribution 0.0029, unseen frequencies
0.0021, learned $c_0 = -0.1619$ (1.8% from $-1/2\pi$); the direct
no-solve control reads 0.122 and 0.658.^[`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`,
key `iteration_2_neumann`.] Changing the boundary condition costs
optimization time, not structure.

![Validation trajectories at the deployment discretization (128
panels, 512 queries). Left, Dirichlet: the 3- and 13-parameter models
cross below the 19k-parameter pair-kernel control before step 1,000
and keep descending. Right, Neumann: validation rises to about 3.4
around step 250 while kernel and solve co-adapt, then descends
monotonically for 10,000 steps. Session artifacts, not checked in.
`figures/convergence_trajectories.png`.](figures/convergence_trajectories.png){#fig-convergence}

The three-parameter model is an oracle-in-family: it exists because
the benchmark PDE is known, and it fixes the ceiling that structure sets
on this problem. The general architecture is measured against it.

### The angular ceiling of separable decoders {#sec-ceiling}

A decoder that contracts query features against pooled boundary moments
cannot represent the Laplace solution operator, for a provable reason.
At an interior query the only query-side vector is the centered position
$x$; a stack that carries scalars and polar vectors can therefore emit,
in linear mode with scalar output, only
$u(x) = c(|x|^2) + b(|x|^2)\cdot x + x^\mathsf T A(|x|^2)\, x$. On any
circle about the model origin the angular content is limited to Fourier
orders $m \le 2$; width, heads, rank and depth add radial structure and
channel multiplicity but cannot create an $m \ge 3$ irreducible
component. The measured pure-mode response is exactly that nullspace.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pure-mode
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Relative L2 response to a single boundary harmonic mode, one mode
#|   at a time (3 seeds, 1,000 updates, 8 geometries per mode). Purple
#|   open markers: MT1 with the separable moment decoder. Grey: the
#|   free-form pair kernel, which forms joint source-query geometry and
#|   degrades smoothly instead. A value of 1.0 means no response. The
#|   moment decoder transmits modes 0-2 and nothing above, although modes
#|   1-4 occur in training. Not shown: the kernel decoder, whose m >= 3
#|   ring content is verified nonzero by a paired random-weight test.
#|   results/reference_2026-07-01.json, block pure_mode_relative_l2.
#| code-fold: true
responses = REF["pure_mode_relative_l2"]
modes = list(range(9))
mt = [responses["mesh_transformer"][str(m)] for m in modes]
pk = [responses["invariant_pair_kernel"][str(m)] for m in modes]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 3.4))
ax.axhline(1.0, color=INK, lw=1.0, ls="--")
ax.text(8.4, 1.02, "no response", fontsize=8, color=INK, ha="right", va="bottom")
ax.axvspan(2.5, 8.5, color=PURPLE, alpha=0.06, lw=0)
ax.text(8.45, 1.22, "proved $m \\geq 3$ nullspace of the moment decoder",
        ha="right", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2)
ax.plot(modes, mt, "o-", color=PURPLE, mfc="white", mec=PURPLE, mew=1.6,
        ms=7, lw=1.4, label="MT1, moment decoder (135,945 p)")
ax.plot(modes, pk, "s-", color=GREY, ms=6, lw=1.4,
        label="free-form pair kernel (19,008 p)")
ax.set_xticks(modes, [f"m={m}" for m in modes])
ax.set_xlabel("boundary harmonic mode (modes 1-4 occur in training)")
ax.set_ylabel("pure-mode relative $L^2$")
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.32)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The ceiling is a property of the source–query factorization, not of
the boundary encoder: replacing the moment decoder by a dense relative
pair decoder improves in-distribution error by 0.34–0.39, while adding
the global encoder to the moment decoder changes it by
0.00026.^[`results/architectural_ablation_2026-07-01.json`.] The kernel-basis
decoder of @sec-kernel-decoder lifts it; the paired random-weight ring
test asserts that the moment decoder's $m \ge 3$ content is
$\le 2\times10^{-11}$ while the kernel decoder's is $\ge 10^{-6}$.

| model (frozen 64-case reference bank, 3,000 updates, 3 seeds) | parameters | ID | unseen frequencies | mode-6 response |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| kernel decoder, full dictionary (singular + polynomial + 8 MLP members) | 110,561 | 0.0399 ± 0.0035 | 0.487 ± 0.047 | 0.48 |
| kernel decoder, singular + polynomial members | 105,089 | 0.0409 ± 0.0076 | **0.0713 ± 0.0008** | 0.064 |
| moment decoder (reference capacity) | 135,945 | 0.4503 ± 0.0016 | 1.000 | 1.00 |
| free-form pair kernel (control) | 19,008 | 0.0398 ± 0.0013 | 0.497 | 0.41 |

: The ceiling and its lift on the reference bank. Every row is trained
for 3,000 updates, which is why the pair kernel reads 0.0398 here rather
than its 1,000-update 0.107. `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, key
`iteration_7_kernel_decoder_fix`. {#tbl-kernel-refbank}

### Dictionary selection {#sec-dictionary-selection}

The unseen-frequency column of @tbl-kernel-refbank contains the finding
the rest of the dictionary evidence turns on. With smooth MLP members
present, unseen-frequency error *worsens with training* (0.12 at 1,000
updates, 0.49 at 3,000) at unchanged in-distribution error; without
them it holds at 0.071. The near-zero-initialized smooth members grow
to absorb residual in-distribution error and slide the kernel toward
value interpolation on unseen right-hand sides. Training trades
structure for interpolation, so the data does not select the structured
members: selection has to be imposed.

#### The dictionary ablations {#sec-dictionary-ablation}

Which members carry the decoder? Four dictionaries at the reference
protocol (3,000 steps, seeds 17/29/43, frozen 64-case banks):

```{python}
#| label: fig-dictionary-ablation
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The four-arm 2D dictionary ablation at identical protocol. Markers
#|   are seeds (circle 17, square 29, triangle 43); horizontal bars are
#|   three-seed means. Top: in-distribution error, where the four arms
#|   are within seed noise of each other and singular-only is best.
#|   Bottom (log scale): unseen-frequency error, where every dictionary
#|   containing MLP members is destroyed and polynomial members amplify
#|   the harm (0.49 with both present, 0.21 with MLP alone); singular-only
#|   matches singular + polynomial. Not shown: the geometry banks, on
#|   which all four arms are within 0.05-0.12.
#|   results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json, keys iteration_7_kernel_decoder_fix
#|   and iteration_11_dictionary_ablation_2d.
#| code-fold: true
it7 = BIE["iteration_7_kernel_decoder_fix"]["reference_bank_3seed_3000steps"]
it11 = BIE["iteration_11_dictionary_ablation_2d"]["runs"]
arms = [
    ("singular + poly + MLP\n(12 members)",
     it7["kernel_full"]["id"], it7["kernel_full"]["freq"]),
    ("singular + MLP\n(9)",
     [r["interpolation"] for r in it11["nopoly"]],
     [r["unseen_boundary_frequencies"] for r in it11["nopoly"]]),
    ("singular + poly\n(4)",
     it7["kernel_dictionary_only"]["id"], it7["kernel_dictionary_only"]["freq"]),
    ("singular only\n(1)",
     [r["interpolation"] for r in it11["singonly"]],
     [r["unseen_boundary_frequencies"] for r in it11["singonly"]]),
]
seed_markers = ["o", "s", "^"]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(7.0, 6.2), sharex=True)
for ax, index, ylabel in [(axes[0], 1, "in-distribution relative $L^2$"),
                          (axes[1], 2, "unseen-frequency relative $L^2$ [log]")]:
    for i, arm in enumerate(arms):
        values = arm[index]
        mean = sum(values) / len(values)
        ax.plot([i - 0.2, i + 0.2], [mean, mean], color=PURPLE, lw=2.4, zorder=2)
        for marker, value in zip(seed_markers, values):
            ax.plot(i, value, marker, ms=8, color=PURPLE, mfc="white",
                    mec=PURPLE, mew=1.5, zorder=3)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
axes[0].set_ylim(0.030, 0.052)
axes[1].set_yscale("log")
axes[1].set_ylim(0.05, 0.7)
axes[1].set_xticks(range(4), [a[0] for a in arms])
axes[1].set_xlim(-0.5, 3.5)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Singular-only is best on every 2D split: in distribution 0.0375, stronger
deformation 0.0774, unseen frequencies 0.0748 with the tightest seed
spread (0.073–0.076), with one member and the fewest parameters
(104,261). The smooth structure of the solution operator is carried
entirely by the operator-conditioned coefficients of the exact singular
member. The interaction by which polynomial members amplify MLP harm is
measured at one capacity and is not explained.

#### Universality: linear everywhere, nonlinearity needs a smooth basis {#sec-singonly-universality}

On screened Laplace (three seeds, 2,000 steps) the one-member
dictionary is again best in class, and the $\tilde\kappa$ conditioning
survives the pruning: the encoder carries the parameter dependence into
the coefficients of a single exact kernel.

| screened arm (3-seed means) | ID | $\tilde\kappa$ below band | $\tilde\kappa$ above band | unseen drive modes |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| singular + 8 MLP members | 0.0144 | 0.0443 | 0.1835 | 0.1842 |
| singular + poly | 0.0120 | 0.0414 | 0.1847 | 0.0192 |
| **singular only** | **0.0099** | **0.0345** | **0.1657** | 0.0206 |

: Screened Laplace by dictionary, 2,000 steps, seeds 17/18/19.
`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, keys
`iteration_9_screened_meshtransformer` and
`iteration_13_singonly_universality`. {#tbl-screened-singonly}

The rule is not universal across field modes. In the
zero-preserving nonlinear field mode used for Liouville's equation, the
same pruning destroys the model (in-distribution 0.96 / 36.5 / 2.30
across seeds, one diverged, against 0.46–0.48 for polynomial-bearing
nonlinear arms; @sec-nonlinear-suites). The rule that survives every
suite: **the dictionary carries the singularity, conditioning carries
the smoothness, nonlinearity needs a smooth basis.** In drive-linear
operation the dictionary is the exact singular member(s) alone; MLP
members are prunable everywhere.

#### The screened suite through the full architecture {#sec-screened}

Two further facts about the screened suite bound what the conditioning
buys. Extrapolating the operator parameter is the weak split: above the
training band the singular-only arm reads 0.166 against 0.010 in
distribution, because conditioning interpolates the parameter dependence
it has seen; below the band it holds 0.035. When the operator *is*
known, the analytic control wins outright: a parameter-free
double-layer solve with the exact modified-Bessel kernel reads
0.00110 in distribution, 0.00060 below the band, 0.0035 above it and
0.0047 on unseen modes over 64 cases per split, 12–66x more accurate
than the singular-only MT1 means and with exact interior operator
conformity.^[`results/screened_canonical_double_layer_2026-07-29_job5689394`.]
MT1's PDE residual $\|(\Delta-\kappa^2)\hat u\|/\|\hat u\|$ on this
suite is 0.5–0.7: it fits the field without satisfying the screened
operator, which is the price of not being handed the kernel.

### 3D results {#sec-3d-results}

MT1 trains on the 3D suite with zero core changes and a
parameter count identical to 2D, because channel counts are
dimension-independent and the only dimension-aware code is the
dictionary's dispatch from subtended angle to solid angle
(@sec-3d-meshtransformer).

On the smooth tiers MT1 sits within 2–6x of the exact-quadrature oracle
and 34–56x below matched Transolver. On the shell the double-layer-only
arms are pinned near 0.37, the size of the winding component they
cannot represent; adding the single-layer member does not fix the shell
at three seeds (0.305 / 0.368 / 0.704) and the Transolver gap narrows to
1.4x. Representation limits bind every architecture there. The 3D
analogue of @sec-pruning holds as well: a two-parameter learned solve
(one coefficient on the exact solid-angle influence, one shared
relaxation, eight steps, and no reference frame since solid angles are
dimensionless) matches the dense oracle to within $3\times10^{-4}$ on
every simply connected tier, with the learned coefficient at $-1.0029$
against the gauge-consistent $-1$.^[Session banks; reported in the setup
block of `iteration_10_laplace3d_meshtransformer`.]

#### The full architecture in 3D {#sec-3d-meshtransformer}

The shell tier's two surfaces are merged into a single boundary mesh,
so boundary identity reaches the model only through positions and
normals. Six seeds of the polynomial-bearing arms establish the
dimensional genericity at 0.017–0.020 on spheres and 0.018–0.027 on
stars (top rows of @tbl-dictionary-3d); the pruned dictionaries halve
those numbers and remove the shell tier's catastrophic seeds.

### The single-layer member and hard geometry {#sec-single-layer}

Two exact singular members are the default dictionary for hard
geometry; the measured cost is worse frequency extrapolation on easy
geometry. The single-layer member adds 276 parameters (104,537 total)
and is validated to $\sim10^{-14}$ against brute-force quadrature. On

stated; the pair-kernel control is the 1,500-step reference):

|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| MT1, singular only | 0.115 | 0.246 | 0.153 | 0.153 |
| **MT1, double + single layer** | **0.065** | **0.160** | **0.102** | **0.087** |
| free-form pair kernel (control) | 0.097 | 0.242 | 0.161 | 0.160 |

: Multi-body family head-to-head. `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`,
key `iteration_16_single_layer_member`, block
`encoder_stress_head_to_head`. {#tbl-multibody}

| deep cavity | ID (2 seeds) | deep slot (3 seeds) | convex control (2 seeds) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| MT1, singular only | 0.098 | 0.393 | 0.083 |

On multiply connected data the single-layer member is decisive: it
wins all twelve split–seed comparisons against singular-only and beats
the pair-kernel control everywhere, and without it MT1 loses to the
pair kernel in distribution (0.115 vs 0.097), exactly where the data
carries winding content the double layer cannot supply. The gate is not
purely topological: the deep cavity is simply connected and the member
still helps (deep slot 0.240 vs 0.393). The cost appears on easy
geometry, where the 2D unseen-frequency error regresses from 0.075 to
0.17–0.27 with the member present. The mechanism is coefficient
freedom: in a classical boundary-integral method the single-layer
density is determined by the boundary system, whereas here it is freely
fit, so on easy domains training spends the member's smooth far field
on interpolation.

## Generalization across boundary conditions {#sec-part-contracts}

Physical structure enters MT1 as declared contracts, and each
declaration makes a falsifiable prediction about which axis of
generalization it buys. On the linear suites three axes were measured:
boundary-data amplitude, boundary-data frequency content, and parity
under reflection. Linearity buys amplitude exactly; the exact kernel
buys frequency content; a typed pseudoscalar channel buys the handed
component. A fourth axis, query radius in exterior problems, is bought
by licensed decay structure.

### Amplitude and frequency content {#sec-bc-generalization}

Four arms at matched parameters (104k–136k) train on the 2D Laplace
suite with drive modes 1–4, boundary RMS 1.0 and deformation bound
$\le 0.3$, three seeds each, identical optimizer and epochs, and are
evaluated on five banks that each move one factor: an in-range control;
drive modes 5–8 with the constant removed; boundary amplitude scaled
2x and 4x; and deformation in $[0.3, 0.6]$. The arms are MT1 with the
singular-only kernel decoder in linear mode; MT1 with the separable
moment decoder in place of the kernel decoder (a control for
@sec-ceiling); MeshTransformer2 (@sec-mt2) with the Dirichlet trace
supplied as an invariant boundary-scalar seed feature; and a plain
soft-slice transformer of the Transolver family. Only the two MT1 arms
declare linearity.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bc-generalization
#| fig-cap: >
```

|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **MT1, exact-kernel decoder** | **0.0158** | **0.0701** (4.4x) | 0.0163 (1.03x) | 0.0154 (0.97x) | **0.0232** (1.46x) |
| MT1, moment decoder (control) | 0.0723 | 1.004 (13.9x) | 0.0667 (0.92x) | 0.0632 (0.87x) | 0.0898 (1.24x) |

`results/g3/g3_reduction_with_kernel.json`. {#tbl-bc-generalization}

**Amplitude extrapolation is exact under declared linearity.** The
relative $L^2$ error is invariant under scaling of a linear model's
input, so the two MT1 arms' amplitude ratios of 0.87–1.03 are sampling
noise around 1. The two arms that must learn the amplitude response pay
6–12x (MT2) and 4.5–7x (soft-slice), worsening with extrapolation
distance. For a linear PDE this is the cheapest contract in the
program: it costs nothing in distribution and removes an axis of
failure.

**Frequency-content generalization is bought by the exact kernel and
nothing else measured.** On drive modes never seen in training the
exact-kernel MT1 reads 0.070, reproducing the 0.075 of the reference
protocol (@tbl-kernel-refbank) under a different training recipe. The
moment-decoder control reads 1.00, which is the proved nullspace of
@sec-ceiling: modes 5–8 with the constant removed are entirely
$m \ge 3$ content. The two soft-slice arms read 1.15 and 1.21, as bad
as or worse than predicting zero. Learned routing must have seen each
mode; an exact Green's-function operator carries the PDE's spectral
response for every mode at once. Declared linearity alone does not buy
this axis: the linear moment-decoder control fails it, and the
stream-factorization ablation below makes the same point on the
reference protocol.

Pricing the operator/drive two-stream separation of MT1
(@sec-stream-factorization) against a single-stream control, in which
the drive is re-declared as operator features with unit-drive
propagation, confirms which contract carries which axis. The control
forfeits the zero-drive and superposition contracts by design and
matches parameters within 0.03%; three seeds, reference protocol:

| 2D Laplace (3-seed means) | ID | unseen geometry | unseen frequencies | zero-drive output | superposition violation |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **two-stream (the architecture)** | **0.0485** | **0.0686** | 0.2111 | **0 (exact)** | **$10^{-7}$** |
| single-stream control | 0.0606 | 0.0813 | **0.1794** | 0.0378 | 0.0421 |

: The stream factorization on 2D Laplace with the two-member
dictionary. "Zero-drive output" is the RMS output at zero boundary data;
"superposition violation" is the relative defect of
$u(g_1 + g_2) - u(g_1) - u(g_2)$. `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`,
key `iteration_26_stream_factorization`. {#tbl-stream-laplace}

The factorization wins in distribution by 3.6 seed standard deviations
at matched parameters and is the only arm with roundoff-exact
contracts; the control learns approximate linearity and plateaus five
decades above the structural value. It does not buy frequency
extrapolation (the control is slightly better there): spectrum
extrapolation lives in the dictionary and its conditioning, not in the
linearity contract. The two-member dictionary used here is why the
unseen-frequency level is 0.21 rather than the one-member 0.075
(@sec-single-layer).

### Parity: the pseudoscalar channel {#sec-pseudo-extension}

Potential flow makes the physics handed: circulation flips sign in a
mirror, so the circulatory part of the velocity field is a pseudoscalar
times a rotated position, a product the scalar-and-polar-vector type
system cannot form. Every untyped arm on the circulation-beyond-training
bank sits on the same floor, 0.645–0.651, the norm of the
unrepresentable vortex component. Adding a 2D pseudoscalar channel type
(wedge $v\wedge w$, rotation $p\cdot v^\perp$, and the two scalar
products that close the set), with circulation declared pseudoscalar,
removes the floor at five seeds (17–21):

| potential-flow velocity (5-seed means) | parameters | ID | unseen geometry | wilder shapes | circulation beyond training | far-field queries |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **MT1, two members + pseudoscalar channels** | 132,641 | **0.028** | **0.041** | **0.131** | **0.037** | 0.673 |
| MT1, full dictionary + pseudoscalar channels | 138,665 | 0.029 | 0.048 | 0.136 | 0.049 | 0.764 |
| untyped velocity arms (pooled controls) | — | 0.141 | 0.191 | 0.264 | 0.647 | 0.83 |

: The pseudoscalar extension at five seeds against the pooled untyped
controls. `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, key
`iteration_23_pseudoscalar_extension`. {#tbl-pseudo-extension-linear}

Circulation-OOD falls 17x and joins the in-distribution level; the whole
velocity field improves about 5x because the handed component was
contaminating every split. The default path is bitwise-preserved at
zero pseudoscalar width, and reflection equivariance of every product is
under test.

### The far field of exterior problems {#sec-farfield-ladder}

Queries beyond the training annulus $[1.05, 4]$ body radii degrade
every potential-flow arm (0.43–0.88; @tbl-pseudo-extension-linear). The cause
is unbounded radial dependence in the learned coefficients, not the
dictionary: the member basis is exactly analytic on $[4, 12]$ while the
prediction super-decays (fitted exponent $-24$ against the exact $-2$),
and the output gate's collapse at the training edge moves with the
annulus when the annulus is widened. Widening the annulus to
$[1.05, 8]$ mitigates (0.694 to 0.179) but leaves the model 6.2x above
its in-distribution error inside the new annulus.

| configuration (seed 17 unless stated) | far-field relative $L^2$ |
|---|--:|
| reference | 0.694 |
| bounded output gate alone | 2.98 |
| bounded gate + compactified query position $x \to x/\sqrt{1+|x|^2}$ fed to the coefficients | 0.452 |
| + exact $r^{-2}$ envelope on the direct drive + monopole-free single layer (5-seed mean) | **0.090 ± 0.048** |

: Far-field error by structural element on potential-flow velocity.
The kernel members are bitwise pinned to raw positions throughout; only
the learned coefficients see bounded inputs.
`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, keys
`iteration_28_bounded_gate` through `iteration_30_decay_structure`.
{#tbl-farfield}

Bounding the gate alone makes the far field 4.3x worse, because the
collapse had been suppressing polynomially growing query-side drive
branches. Bounding the coefficients' inputs at the source excludes
coefficient extrapolation by construction (coefficient traces flat to
$r = 12$) and isolates the residual as representational: a bounded
direct branch converges to a direction-dependent constant where the
exact field decays as $r^{-2}$. Two zero-parameter structures the
physics licenses for zero-net-flux exteriors close it: an exact
$1/(1+|x|^2)$ envelope on the direct drive (the leading exterior term is
the doublet), and a measure-weighted rank-one deflation of the
single-layer column that gives exact zero net charge for any
coefficients and, as a corollary, cancels the 2D log gauge. The
five-seed result is 0.090 ± 0.048 (per-seed 0.036–0.147) at an unchanged
training annulus, with every other split at family-best levels (ID
0.0174, circulation 0.0168, unseen geometry 0.0303). One leak remains
fitted rather than exact: the $r^{-1}$ member tails cancel to $r^{-2}$
only through learned zero-circulation cancellation.

## What the encoder contributes {#sec-global-flow}

For the Dirichlet problem $u(x) = \int_\Gamma g\, d\omega_x$ with
harmonic measure $\omega_x$ whose density depends on the whole domain,
so every boundary patch influences every interior point and no cutoff
radius survives a change of geometry. MT1 therefore uses all-to-all
boundary attention with no neighborhoods. How much of that attention
the linear suites need is a measured question, and the answer is: very
little for all-Dirichlet problems, one layer where the boundary solve is
nonlocal, one head everywhere, and vector channels off easy geometry.

### The hard-geometry families {#sec-encoder-stress}

On a deformed disk two boundary points close in $\mathbb R^2$ are close
along the boundary, so a kernel of pairwise invariants never has to see
around geometry. Two families remove that convenience, both with
exterior-charge exact labels and unit-RMS boundary traces, every sample
certified at build time (queries inside, charges outside, curves
non-self-intersecting, bodies disjoint). **Multi-body**: a disk minus
two disjoint disks, three boundaries merged into one mesh, with charges
biased toward the gap-facing surfaces so that in the narrow-gap regime
the trace on one body is dominated by a charge hidden inside the other.
**Deep cavity**: a disk with a deep, narrow, filleted slot and charges
nestled in the slot, so opposite slot walls are Euclidean-close while
the field between them is mediated by the whole cavity. The free-form
pair kernel is the essential control: it is exactly the class that sees
only pair invariants.

The control's reading in @tbl-multibody and @tbl-deepcavity is
moderate. The pair kernel is competitive with singular-only MT1 on
every hard split and loses to the two-member MT1 by 1.1–1.8x; the
families are a separation dial, and how much pair-blindness costs is
what the control measures, not a theorem.

### Encoder depth {#sec-encoder-depth}

On the all-Dirichlet multi-body family, zero boundary self-attention
layers (59,385 parameters) match the full two-layer two-member model at
two seeds (seed 17: 0.073 vs 0.070 in distribution; seed 18: 0.067
against the three-seed mean 0.065).^[`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`,
key `iteration_18_encoder_depth`.] This is the expected result: the Dirichlet double-layer density solves a
second-kind Fredholm system dominated by the local $\tfrac12 I$ term, so
the boundary-to-boundary solve is nearly local even though the
boundary-to-interior map is not.

### Where attention matters: mixed boundary conditions {#sec-mixed-bc}

A mixed Cauchy solve is nonlocal: unknown Dirichlet data on one surface
must be inferred from Neumann data on another. The shell tier with the
inner surface carrying the trace and the outer carrying the flux is the
one mixed tier the generator permits. Three encoder depths, 3,000
steps, seeds 17/18/19, on the mixed shell bank and a finer-resolution
copy of it:

| boundary self-attention layers | parameters | seed 17 | seed 18 | seed 19 | mean | finer resolution (mean) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 | 104,713 | 0.0479 | 0.0374 | 0.0614 | 0.049 | 0.070 |
| 1 | 82,137 | 0.0534 | 0.0423 | 0.0576 | 0.051 | 0.060 |
| 0 | 59,561 | 0.0612 | 0.1120 | 0.0650 | 0.079 | 0.102 |

: The mixed-boundary-condition depth sweep on the shell tier.
`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, key
`iteration_19_mixed_bc_discriminator`. {#tbl-mixed-bc}

Without attention the mixed problem degrades (0.079 vs 0.049) and the
failure mode is unreliability rather than uniform loss: one seed reads
0.112, and 0.182 at the finer resolution. One layer matches two (0.051
vs 0.049), so the reference configuration carries one. The mixed shell
at 0.049 is also 7x easier than the all-Dirichlet shell (0.37):
handing the model the outer flux removes the winding-inference
difficulty. Caveats: a single mixed geometry tier, and the drive blocks
were held at one layer in every arm, so a drive-depth sweep remains the
sharper follow-up.

### Heads versus rank at fixed score capacity {#sec-heads-vs-rank}

Per attention head the effective score matrix has rank at most
$R_0 + D R_1$ ($R_0$ scalar rank, $R_1$ vector rank, $D$ the spatial
dimension), so one layer's pair-coefficient class is fixed by the total
$H(R_0 + D R_1)$. Heads remain distinct after the scores because the
value maps are head-blocked. Three two-member arms hold the total at 80
on the 2D Laplace reference bank (3,000 steps, seeds 17/29/43); the
pre-registered rule counts a three-seed mean within twice the larger seed
standard deviation as a match:

| arm | $H$ | $R_0/R_1$ | parameters | ID | unseen geometry | stronger deformation | unseen frequencies |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| reference | 4 | 12/4 | 104,537 | 0.0485 ± 0.0025 | 0.0686 ± 0.0070 | 0.0862 ± 0.0148 | 0.2111 ± 0.0523 |
| one head | 1 | 48/16 | 104,123 | **0.0413 ± 0.0021** | 0.0624 ± 0.0018 | 0.0825 ± 0.0058 | 0.1831 ± 0.0158 |
| eight heads | 8 | 6/2 | 104,897 | 0.0461 ± 0.0014 | 0.0669 ± 0.0041 | 0.0812 ± 0.0147 | 0.2077 ± 0.0471 |

: Heads traded against separable ranks at fixed total score capacity
$H(R_0 + 2R_1) = 80$; bold marks the one cell outside the pre-registered
tolerance. `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, key
`iteration_31_heads_vs_rank`. {#tbl-heads-vs-rank}

Eight heads at halved ranks are bookkeeping: every split matches. One
full-width head wins in distribution (0.0413 vs 0.0485, 2.9 seed
standard deviations), is directionally better on all four splits, the
most seed-stable, and the smallest. Because the score class was matched
exactly, the gain prices the head-blocking of the value and output maps.

### One head across suites {#sec-one-head-cross-suite}

The same capacity-preserving trade (heads 4 to 1, ranks 12/4 to 48/16)
was then run at three seeds on screened Laplace, potential-flow velocity
with the pseudoscalar sector, and 3D Laplace against the archived
four-head comparators, with a pre-registered rule for a default change:
flip to one head if every split of at least two suites matches or beats
and no split anywhere is a decisive loss. Thirteen of thirteen
suite–split cells match or beat, all three suites pass, and the
reference configuration is one head (81,547
parameters).^[`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, key
`iteration_32_one_head_cross_suite`.] The Laplace in-distribution win
did not travel: one head is directionally worse on 11 of 13 cells (both
exceptions are unseen-mode splits), so the cross-suite evidence is
non-inferiority and the flip is carried by parsimony. The tolerance keys
to the larger of the two arms' seed spreads, which favors the noisier
arm; three seeds bound this as within-tolerance ties, not equivalence.

### Are the vector channels essential? {#sec-scalar-only}

Scalar-only mode removes oriented state transport between cells: the
latent state carries no vector channels, though normals still enter
through the decoder's pair invariants and scalar Gram invariants at the
lift. Parameters drop about 60% (104,261 to 41,941 for singular-only).

| suite / split (3-seed means) | scalar-only | vector-ful | ratio |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2D Laplace ID | 0.0400 | 0.0375 | 1.07x |
| 2D Laplace, unseen frequencies | 0.0733 | 0.0748 | 0.98x |
| screened ID | 0.0283 | 0.0099 | 2.9x |
| 3D sphere | 0.0244 | 0.0072 | 3.4x |
| 3D star | 0.0228 | 0.0121 | 1.9x |
| 3D star, unseen modes | 0.0524 | 0.0637 | 0.8x |
| 3D shell | 0.373 | 0.377 | 1.0x |

: Scalar-only against the vector-ful singular-only reference; ratio is
scalar-only error over vector-ful error. The shell row compares the
scalar-only mean with the vector-ful six-seed median.
`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, key `iteration_14_scalar_only_2d`.
{#tbl-scalar-only}

On plain 2D Laplace the vector channels are not needed: scalar-only
matches within 5–15% on every split at 60% fewer parameters, and
similarity covariance stays at $2.5$–$2.8\times10^{-7}$, so equivariance
never depended on them. Off that suite they are physics capacity:
in-distribution error degrades 2–3.4x, and a capacity-matched wide
scalar control (105,301 parameters) does not recover it (3D sphere 0.024,
screened 0.024). The gap is oriented transport, not width. The shell
tier and unseen-mode splits are indifferent, consistent with the shell
error being representational (@sec-single-layer).

## Discretization and units invariance as measured {#sec-invariances-measured}

The four properties a boundary-driven surrogate should have are defined
in @sec-four-properties; the linear suites measure two of them
directly.

**Discretization: refinement converges, subsampling does not.** Holding
one sphere fixed and refining an icosphere tiling (coverage always
100%), the operator's error against its converged limit falls 2.51% to
0.59% to 0.12% as each subdivision quadruples the cell count, at or
slightly better than second order. Zero-shot resolution transfer on
trained models shows the same behavior: the kernel-decoder MT1 trained
at 64 panels in 2D improves from 0.322 to 0.032 as evaluation goes from
32 to 256 panels (the moment decoder is flat at 0.27), and the
three-parameter learned solve improves monotonically over the same
range (@sec-pruning). In 3D:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-resolution-3d
#| output: asis
#| code-fold: true
scale = BIE["iteration_20_scale_ladder"]["a100"]["resolution_transfer_zero_shot"]
lines = ["| tier | subdivision 2 (trained) | subdivision 3 | subdivision 4 |",
         "|---|--:|--:|--:|"]
for tier in ("sphere", "star"):
    vals = [scale[f"{tier}_subdiv{s}"] for s in (2, 3, 4)]
    lines.append(f"| {tier} | " + " | ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in vals) + " |")
lines.append(
    ": Zero-shot resolution transfer of the one-layer two-member MT1 "
    "(81,961 parameters) trained at subdivision 2 and evaluated without "
    "retraining across a 16x range of boundary cell count. Mild degradation, "
    "no collapse. `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, key "
    "`iteration_20_scale_ladder`. {#tbl-resolution-3d}")
print("\n".join(lines))
```

Random decimation of a fixed mesh is a different experiment: retaining
a random 1.6–25% of cells leaves 32–9% error against the full-coverage
operator, concentrated deep in the interior (222% at the sphere center
against 0.3% at the wall), and no reweighting of the retained cells
recovers a missing global integral. The linear suites always present
the full boundary; industrial pipelines that train on sparse point
samples do not (@sec-limits).

**Units invariance in length.** The reference length is derived from
the geometry itself (the measure-weighted RMS boundary radius,
@sec-intrinsic-gauge). At three seeds on the reference bank this is
accuracy-neutral (in-distribution 0.0372 against 0.0375 with an
explicit length key; unseen frequencies 0.0750 against 0.0748), and
paired similarity covariance is $2.9$–$3.1\times10^{-7}$ including
0.2x and 5x rescalings. Corrupting an explicit length key by 3x at
evaluation degrades the explicit-key model 4.64x; the intrinsic-gauge
model is bitwise unaffected because the input no longer
exists.^[`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`, key
`iteration_24_intrinsic_gauge`.] Quadrature weighting against boundary
measure is checked as an exact test: splitting a panel into
measure-conserving duplicates leaves the moment operators algebraically
unchanged.

## Where the linear line stops {#sec-pde-agnostic}

Every result above depends on one fact: the fundamental solution of the
governing operator was known, so its singular member could be integrated
exactly and placed in the dictionary. What transfers to problems where
the operator is not given is narrower.

PDE-agnostic, and carried into every later architecture in this book:
the factorization of the solution operator into a boundary-to-boundary
solve composed with a source-to-query propagation; the second-kind
solve structure with its gauge rule (@sec-neumann); the exact contracts
(linearity where the physics is linear, similarity covariance,
quadrature weighting against measure, all-to-all information flow,
query independence); kernels that are functions of the joint invariants
of $\{x - y,\ n_y,\ \text{boundary vector data}\}$, the one strong
structural assumption a homogeneous problem class licenses; and the
singular-quadrature discipline, since whatever the kernel family is, its
near-boundary singular structure must be integrated, not sampled
(@tbl-h1e).

PDE-specific, available on these benchmarks and not in deployment: the
fundamental-solution family itself, and with it exact operator
conformity and the maximum-principle bound on interior error. On
screened Laplace the known-operator control is 12–66x more accurate
than MT1 (@sec-screened); on the shell tier the double layer's flux
deficiency binds MT1 and Transolver alike (@tbl-3d).

Three places mark the end of the linear line. Drive-nonlinear problems
break the singular-only rule and need both a smooth basis and a
declared drive degree (@sec-nonlinear-suites, @sec-nonlinear-fragility).
On separated 3D aerodynamics the potential-flow prior fails outright: a
potential-flow oracle for interior pressure on DrivAerML reads 4.8
against 0.77 for predicting the case mean, and the exact double-layer
decoder is 8x behind GeoTransolver on the interior task (@sec-interior);
on industrial surfaces the kernel dictionary contributes 0–8% and the
trace formulation carries the gain (@sec-industrial-mt1). Exact spectral
response from an exact Green's-function operator is a statement about
linear boundary-value problems with known operators; what replaces it
when the operator is unknown is the subject of the rest of the book.
